title: Progressive Degradation for Hosted Inference Surface PRD + Launch Checklist
creator: Sanjay Malik
description: Objective: Define and ship a Progressive Degradation policy and implementation for the Redwood hosted inference surface so customer applications stay functional (with predictable quality/cost trade-offs) when capacity or latency targets are threatened. This PRD covers behavior for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints, the API error/fallback contracts, console/operator controls, and the launch readiness checklist.
goals: Maintain availability of hosted endpoints under capacity pressure by falling back deterministically to compatible model variants or degraded modes
Expose clear, stable signals to customers (response headers, error codes, Console indicators) describing degradation mode and expected quality impact
Provide operator/tenant controls (policy, thresholds, opt-out) in Console and API keys to tune trade-offs per customer tier
Ensure observable metrics, eval gating, and automated rollback so regressions in quality or cost are detected rapidly
non_goals: Re-architecting serving runtime internals; engineering will implement minimal runtime adapters and use existing kernel selection where possible
Making behavior custom per-customer beyond toggles and per-tenant policies in Console (no bespoke model onboarding for canary customers in v1)
Changing API surface drastically — prefer non-breaking extensions and clear deprecation path if additions required
user_personas: Early-stage product engineer using hosted API with bursty traffic who needs high availability over perfect generation quality
Enterprise platform team requiring control over degradation policy and auditability
SRE/Oncall team that needs clear alerts, playbooks and automated rollback for quality regressions
requirements: R1: Degradation Modes: support (a) model-variant fallback (e.g., opt for smaller/quantized model), (b) feature degradation (disable streaming or function-calls), (c) passive latency-based shedding (reject large requests with 413-like error) and (d) embedding approximate-mode (lower-dim or hashed embeddings)

R2: Contract Signals: responses must include X-Redwood-Degradation header (mode, reason, variant) and standard status codes (200 with warning header, 429 with 'retry-after' for rate shedding, 503 for total outage). Provide structured error body with 'degradation' field when applicable

R3: Endpoint-specific behavior: Chat/completions support streaming continuation fallback to non-streaming with a sticky header; Embeddings should support an 'approximate=true' parameter that returns lower-dimension vectors and a header indicating vector schema; Rerank endpoints can return a best-effort score plus a flag 'approximate_scores' when using a cheaper model
R4: Policy Controls: Console UI and API config must allow per-tenant default policy (aggressive|balanced|conservative), per-route overrides, and an opt-out toggle for critical customers

R5: Eval & Quality Gates: before enabling a degradation variant in production, run eval suite on a representative prompt set (thresholds: chat Bleu-like proxy >= 0.92 of baseline; embeddings cosine recall >= 0.88) and capture results in the release artifact

R6: Telemetry: emit metrics for degradation activations, per-tenant fallback counts, per-model latency distributions, quality-regression alerts tied to eval sets, and cost-per-request delta when degraded
R7: SDK/Docs: SDKs must gracefully surface degradation headers to developers and console docs must include migration notes, examples and recommended prompts to reduce sensitivity to degradation
R8: Rollout: support canary (1% traffic), staged ramp (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> global) with automatic rollback conditions (quality alert or error budget burn rate > 50% over 10m)
R9: Backwards Compatibility: keep existing endpoint parameters working; any new parameters (e.g., approximate=true) default to false
R10: Security/Audit: all policy changes and degradations must be logged to audit trail with actor and timestamp; KMS does not change
api_contract_changes: Add optional query/body parameter 'approximate' (boolean) to embeddings and rerank endpoints
Introduce response header 'X-Redwood-Degradation' with value form 'mode:variant:reason' and structured description in docs
Return structured 'degradation' object in JSON body when a non-transparent degradation occurred (list of fields must be documented)
Preserve existing status codes but document when 429 vs 503 vs 200+warning are used
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Under a simulated capacity pressure test, 95% of requests are served by a fallback variant rather than returning hard errors for the balanced policy
AC2: Console shows live degradation state and the per-tenant policy UI can change policy that takes effect within 60s
AC3: SDKs surface X-Redwood-Degradation header via language idiomatic interfaces and tests verify header presence when degradation is active
AC4: Eval results for each degradation variant meet thresholds defined in R5 and are recorded in the release artifact before rollout
AC5: Alerts: a quality-regression alert fires within 5 minutes of a threshold breach and initiates automated rollback when configured
AC6: Documentation: API reference updated with examples for approximate=true and explanation of header/body signals; migration guide published
AC7: Security: policy changes are captured in audit logs and accessible in Console history view
AC8: Load test: canary ramp procedure runs successfully (1% -> 10% within config limits) with automated guardrails preventing ramp past 10% if error budget violated
AC9: Post-launch measurement: cost-per-token decreases by >= 8% during high-pressure windows for balanced policy customers without increasing unhandled error rate
privacy_and_security_considerations: Degraded/approximate embeddings may be lower-dimensional; we must add a warning in the data retention/privacy document that approximate vectors still fall under customer data handling policies
Audit logs for policy toggles must be retained per compliance TTL configured by customer; encryption remains unchanged
Security review required for header/body changes to ensure no leakage of internal routing topology
dependencies: ENG-35502 (telemetry: new metrics for degradation activations)
DES-1542 (Console: policy controls and audit UI)
ENG-36020 (SDK: surface degradation headers across languages)
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Quality regression for sensitive customers. Mitigation: conservative default policy, per-tenant opt-out and eval gating before rollout.
Risk: Customer confusion from new headers. Mitigation: SDKs translate headers to structured flags and docs include migration examples.
Risk: Increased operational complexity. Mitigation: limited v1 modes (model-variant and approximate) and strong observability and runbooks.
rollout_checklist: 1. Engineering: runtime adapter PR merged and integration tests green (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7542)
2. Telemetry: metrics and dashboards created (link: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/Degradation) and alertplaybook attached
3. Design: Console policy controls UI implemented and accessibility reviewed (DES-1542)
4. SDKs: Node/Python/Go releases packaged with tests for header exposure (ENG-36020)
5. QA: chaos and capacity-pressure scenarios executed against staging with synthetic traffic and results logged
6. Security: API change review complete and signed off by security (SEC-78)
7. Product: release notes and migration guide published in Docs (link: https://confluence.redwood.com/pages/progressive-degradation)
8. Legal/Compliance: endorsement for audit log retention and privacy implications
9. Canary: enable 1% traffic in a narrow region for 24h with live monitoring
10. Ramp: automated ramp schedule configured (1% -> 10% -> 50%) with guardrails and rollback hooks
11. Post-launch: 72h observation window and quality batting—collect customer feedback and run evals on live traffic samples
qa_and_test_plan: Unit tests for header generation and parsing in SDKs
Integration tests for each endpoint verifying fallback to smaller models and approximate embeddings
Performance tests under load to validate 95th/99th latency SLOs during degradation
A/B evaluation harness that compares baseline vs degraded variant across representative prompt sets
User acceptance tests involving a set of internal beta customers exercising opt-out and policy toggles
metrics_and_success_signALS: Availability: target 99.95% successful responses (200/200+warning) during pressure windows for balanced policy customers
Quality: eval thresholds from R5 must hold in production sampled audits
Cost: per-token cost delta during pressure windows must meet target (>=8% savings for balanced policy)
Operational: degradation-trigger rate and rollback rate tracked; rollback triggers < 5% of activation events after 30 days
